slides.texte_overlay:
How to stop being a pushover
(without becoming a jerk)
Know what you think before you're asked. Five minutes a day of history, art or science builds real opinions. People push around the guy who has none. They listen to the guy who knows things.
slides.texte_sophia: I started doing five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Having real opinions changed everything. People push around the guy who has none.

slides.texte_overlay: Stop saying sorry for things that aren't your fault. "Sorry, can I ask a question?" No. Just ask the question. Saving your apologies for real mistakes makes them mean something when you do say them.
Give yourself time before saying yes. "Let me check and get back to you." Most people say yes on the spot and regret it for weeks. A small delay lets you agree only to what you actually want.
Stop over-explaining your choices. "I'm staying in tonight." You don't need a doctor's note. The more reasons you give, the more people think they can argue with you until you change your mind.
Ask for what you're owed. The money a friend borrowed, the hours your boss promised. "Hey, just checking on that." Polite, short, direct. People respect someone who follows up without getting angry.
Let people be a little disappointed. Not everyone will like your no, and that's fine. You can be kind and still say no. Their reaction isn't your job, as long as you were honest and polite about it.
Stop laughing at jokes that are really insults. A flat "Not funny, man" with a calm face is enough. You don't need to fight. You just need to stop pretending you're fine with being the punchline.
